G50 BMW 3 Series Virtually Spawns a Fresh Angel Eye GT Version, And It Lacks the Neue Klasse DNA
1 photo
Photo: Timur Altynbayev / Behance
The premium German automaker from Bavaria, BMW , is in the middle of one of its largest product offensives in modern times, which began last fall with the introduction of the second-gen NA5 BMW iX3 Neue Klasse compact electric crossover SUV. Now, the avalanche is raging…
So, the tidal wave continued this spring with the release of the NA0 battery electric compact executive car – the second-generation BMW i3 – offered as a sedan and a member of the Neue Klasse pack. These two have all the Neue Klasse goodies: outside, inside, and the dedicated EV platform. There’s also the brand-new NA7 first-ever BMW iX4 coupe-SUV that just joined them earlier this month.
As for the other novelties, they’re partial Neue Klasse models because they were kept on the enhanced CLAR platform for various motives. The latter include the mid-cycle refresh of the BMW 7 Series and i7, the all-new BMW X5 (G65) mid-size crossover SUV with no less than five different powertrains (gas, diesel, PHEV, BEV, and FCEV), or the G50 BMW 3 Series, the eighth generation of the compact executive model.
Additional Neue Klasse novelties are incoming, such as the recently leaked BMW i3 Touring, the often-spied BMW 5 Series facelift, or the BMW M5 and M3, with the latter model set to be offered both with ICE and EV options, potentially even before the end of the year. Speaking of the BMW 3 Series and the M3, a lot of people are either loving or hating the Neue Klasse DNA, though many had great words to say about the new M350 xDrive that has exclusive yellow daytime running lights plus the evolved 3.0-liter B58 turbo inline-six engine under the hood churning out no less than 437 hp now.
Of course, even the rumor mill participated in the conversation, and so did the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI – even if some of them did it a bit later than others. One such example is the virtual artist Timur Altynbayev , who is from Kazakhstan, but his latest unofficial, hypothetical design projects feel targeted at the Bavarian areas of Munich more than anything else.
He recently took upon himself to redesign the G50 BMW 3 Series, the M350 xDrive to be more precise, in an unofficial, hypothetical design project. His idea was simple: he used the Neue Klasse illuminated kidneys from the latest X5 along with dual round LED surround daytime running lights and bigger plus shorter LED taillights to reference the legendary E30 BMW M3 coupe classic allure. Then he also went overboard with a CGI BMW M3 with all-yellow LED lights at the front and a bonkers aerodynamic package, of course.
But now he’s relaxed once again, and claims that “one of the most beautiful bodies BMW had” was the GT variant of its main BMW 5, 6, and 3 Series – which is a point of contention, since a lot of people would also argue that they were, in fact, some of the ugliest versions. Anyway, beauty is always in the eye of the beholder, and the pixel master wants to bring back the discontinued body style.
As such, his latest vision regarding the BMW 3 Series this time around has to do with a digital remake of the BMW 3 Series GT. He deployed the round headlights with LED ‘angel eye’ daytime running lamps from the M350 xDrive and also put a wide kidney grille, which is also functional since this is a 340i version, then added the sloping roof from the iX4 coupe- SUV model and, around the back, put a new trunk lid stolen from the 6 GT with slimmer full-width lights. So, what do you think? Cool or not? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Timur Altynbayev (@timur_altynbayev) View this post on Instagram A post shared by Timur Altynbayev (@timur_altynbayev)
